study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized cerebellar damage predicts the presence of behavioral disorders in children with brainstem tumors

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: 849 healthy children from 4 sites: (1) 72 locally recruited children in Beijing (61 scanned); (2) 69 from fcon_1000.projects dataset; (3) 450 from Child Connectome Project (CCNP/devCCNP); (4) 269 from Children's Hospital in Guangzhou. Additionally, 147 patients with brainstem tumors from Beijing Tiantan Hospital were enrolled for clinical application.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "data from 849 healthy children (age range: 4-18 years) were collected from publicly available databases, including 72 locally recruited children in Beijing (61 of whom underwent scanning), 69 from the fcon_1000.projects dataset (https://doi.org/10.15387/fcp_indi.corr.ipcas7), 450 from the Child Connectome Project (CCNP), and 269 from the Children's Hospital in Guangzhou."

answer.Beijing Tiantan Hospital (patients): clinical application (deviation analysis and behavioral prediction)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: All 849 healthy children data from 4 sites were used to establish normative models with 10-fold cross-validation, then definitive models for deviation analysis in patients. The 147 patients were used for clinical research to assess individual cerebellar volume deviations and predict behavioral disorders.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we established normative models with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), incorporating age and gender as covariates. ... We initially estimated models with 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy children dataset, then developed definitive models for deviation analysis in patients."
